title: Araripe site alert index, version 1
description: The document the public alerts page reads to learn which runs exist, how big each one was, and which object to fetch for each view. It is DERIVED from a green release, never sealed inside one: `release_prefix` is a function of the ledger alone, so publishing this as a `date_product` would make any later change to a statistic threshold collide with its own immutable prefix (SITE_ARTIFACT_CONTRACT_V1.md). Its integrity argument is reproducibility — immutable inputs plus a pure function plus the conformance vectors — not a stored checksum. Every field in `totals` is an aggregation of `runs[]` and nothing else, which is what lets a consumer verify the whole document without reading a single alert feature.

stats_policy_version.description: Which version of the statistics policy produced these numbers. Present because this document is derived rather than sealed: without it, two indexes built by different threshold generations would be indistinguishable. Bumped by src/publication/site_artifact.py whenever a threshold or a derivation changes.

runs.description: One row per UTC date in the release, in chronological order. The order is not re-established here — the release's own `dates[]` is required to be chronological, so an unordered index means the composer re-sorted or the release is malformed, and check_alert_index refuses it rather than repairing it.

strong_points_file.description: Name of the point index the map loads for the all-runs view. It is a build artifact written beside this index by the same green step, NOT a release object, so it is resolved against the index's own location and never against object_base.

last_run.description: The date of the last row in `runs[]`. Null only for an index with no runs, which is a legitimate state before the first release and never to be collapsed into an error.

source.description: Human-readable provenance line shown beside the latest detection date. Free text on purpose: it is a caption, and constraining it here would make a wording fix a contract change.

object_base.description: Mount the per-run objects are served from, prepended to `file`/`file_strong`. It is `/data/green/` for the route Package 2B.4A built, so `/data/green/` + `alerts/run-2026-04-04.geojson` is exactly the request that route resolves. Required, and NOT defaulted: an index that did not say where its objects live would leave the page guessing, and the wrong guess is a 404 on the default view. The per-run objects are never copied into the deploy — they stay in the immutable release, which is the whole reason the 25 MiB per-asset limit and the 247 MiB of committed history stop being the site's problem.

object_name.description: One path segment, for a file that sits BESIDE the index rather than inside the release: the point index is computed by the same green step that writes the index, so it is not a release object and is resolved against the index's own location, never against object_base.

file.description: Logical path of the full run object in the release: every candidate alert for the date.

file_strong.description: Logical path of the strong subset object. A different object from `file`, and check_alert_index refuses an index where the two are equal — collapsing them would serve every candidate under the default view.

count.description: Features with a Polygon or MultiPolygon geometry. NOT the length of the feature array: a feature of any other type carries no area and is skipped, and the difference is a number the page displays.

area_ha.description: Sum of feature areas in hectares, rounded once to one decimal. The rounding is contractual, not cosmetic: `totals.area_ha` sums these rounded values, so a consumer that rounded later would report a different total for the same release.

low.description: Also absorbs any label the policy does not name, including a missing one — the conservative direction, since an unlabelled feature must not be presented as high confidence.

first_obs.description: Seen once. Together with `candidate` and `confirmed` this is a partition of `count`, and the validator enforces the partition rather than trusting it.

strong.description: High confidence AND a streak of at least two sightings AND majority natural vegetation at 10 m. Cannot exceed `high`, which the validator checks.

pcount_max.description: Largest sighting streak on the date, floored at 1. It feeds a UI slider whose range must not collapse on an empty run, and it is carried per run so that `totals.pcount_max` is an aggregation rather than a second pass over the features.

totals.description: Aggregations of `runs[]`. Deliberately NOT a superset of the per-run keys: `medium` and `low` are shown per run and not in aggregate, and adding them here would imply a page element that does not exist.

logical_path.description: A path inside the release prefix, as the release declares it. Same shape as the release contract's logical_path: no absolute path, no traversal, no backslash, no trailing slash. It may contain `/`, unlike the sibling names below, because it is the release's own path and the run assembler chooses its prefix.
